blocks.text: Compose creates a user-defined bridge `<project>_default`, attaches every service, and embedded DNS resolves each service name, so services talk via `service:containerPort` with no `ports:` needed.

items: api → `db:5432`; `ports:` is only for host access.
`--scale worker=3` → one name, three IPs (round-robin); container_name blocks scaling.

blocks.text: proxy can't reach db; db has no internet. Don't mark a network internal if a service on it needs external APIs.

blocks.code:
networks:
  shared: { external: true, name: shared }    # docker network create shared

blocks.text: Listing `networks:` on a service removes it from `default` unless you include `default` too. A classic "name not resolved".

Q: "How do Compose services find each other?" A: "Compose attaches them to a project network with embedded DNS, so each service name resolves to its container(s). Clients use the service name and the container port; published ports are only for the host."

items: Segment with multiple networks; internal: true for DBs.
Explicit networks: drop you from default.
